knowledge_tree.title: English Grade 8 Semester 1
knowledge_tree.content: Comprehensive English language learning for eighth graders, covering themes like holidays, home life, comparisons, nature, food, future plans, technology, and communication.

children.title: Unit 1: Happy Holiday
children.content: Focuses on holiday activities, experiences, and the use of indefinite pronouns.

children.title: Holiday Activities
children.content: Common activities people do during holidays, such as traveling, attending festivals, and relaxing.

children.title: Visiting Relatives
children.content: Spending time with family members during holidays.

children.title: Attending Festivals
children.content: Participating in cultural or seasonal festivals.

children.title: Indefinite Pronouns
children.content: Pronouns like someone, anyone, everyone, nothing, etc., used to refer to non-specific people or things.

children.title: Usage in Questions
children.content: Using indefinite pronouns in questions to ask about experiences.

children.title: Usage in Statements
children.content: Using indefinite pronouns in positive and negative statements.

children.title: Holiday Experiences
children.content: Sharing personal stories and lessons learned from holidays.

children.title: Writing a Holiday Diary
children.content: Describing events and feelings in a diary format.

children.title: Learning from Travel
children.content: Understanding cultural and historical insights gained from traveling.

children.title: Unit 2: Home Sweet Home
children.content: Discusses household chores, making polite requests, and the meaning of home.

children.title: Household Chores
children.content: Tasks done to maintain a home, like cleaning, cooking, and organizing.

children.title: Common Chores
children.content: Examples include sweeping, washing dishes, and making beds.

children.title: Chores Frequency
children.content: How often chores are done and by whom.

children.title: Polite Requests
children.content: Using can and could to ask for permission or make requests politely.

children.title: Asking for Permission
children.content: Using Can I...? or Could I...? to request allowance to do something.

children.title: Making Requests
children.content: Using Can you...? or Could you...? to ask someone to do something.

children.title: Meaning of Home
children.content: Exploring emotional and cultural aspects of what makes a home.

children.title: Family Traditions
children.content: Customs and practices that define family life at home.

children.title: Home as a Safe Space
children.content: The concept of home being a place of comfort and security.

children.title: Unit 3: Same or Different?
children.content: Focuses on making comparisons, discussing similarities and differences, and the value of diversity.

children.title: Comparatives
children.content: Grammar for comparing two things using -er and more.

children.title: Forming Comparatives
children.content: Rules for adding -er or using more with adjectives.

children.title: Irregular Comparatives
children.content: Exceptions like better, worse, etc.

children.title: Similarities and Differences
children.content: Discussing how people are alike and different.

children.title: Physical Comparisons
children.content: Comparing height, appearance, etc.

children.title: Personality Traits
children.content: Comparing characteristics like shyness, outgoingness, etc.

children.title: Value of Diversity
children.content: Understanding why differences are important in friendships and society.

children.title: Learning from Others
children.content: How differences can lead to personal growth.

children.title: Respecting Differences
children.content: The importance of tolerance and acceptance.

children.title: Unit 4: Amazing Plants and Animals
children.content: Explores remarkable plants and animals, superlatives, and human-nature connections.

children.title: Superlatives
children.content: Grammar for comparing three or more things using -est and most.

children.title: Forming Superlatives
children.content: Rules for adding -est or using most with adjectives.

children.title: Irregular Superlatives
children.content: Exceptions like best, worst, etc.

children.title: Remarkable Species
children.content: Learning about unique plants and animals like blue whales, bamboo, etc.

children.title: Blue Whale
children.content: The largest animal on Earth, its habitat, and diet.

children.title: Bamboo
children.content: A fast-growing plant with cultural significance and multiple uses.

children.title: Human-Nature Connection
children.content: How humans and nature are interdependent.

children.title: Ecosystem Roles
children.content: The importance of species like bees in pollination.

children.title: Conservation
children.content: Why protecting plants and animals is crucial.

children.title: Unit 5: What a Delicious Meal!
children.content: Covers food, cooking instructions, adverbs of sequence, and exclamatory sentences.

children.title: Cooking Instructions
children.content: Using imperative verbs to give step-by-step cooking directions.

children.title: Sequencing Adverbs
children.content: Words like first, next, then, finally to order steps.

children.title: Recipe Language
children.content: Common terms used in recipes, e.g., chop, mix, bake.

children.title: Exclamatory Sentences
children.content: Sentences expressing strong emotion with What or How.

children.title: What + Noun Phrase
children.content: e.g., What a beautiful day!

children.title: How + Adjective/Adverb
children.content: e.g., How delicious!

children.title: Food and Culture
children.content: How food reflects cultural traditions and memories.

children.title: Traditional Dishes
children.content: Foods that are part of cultural heritage, like pumpkin pie.

children.title: Food Memories
children.content: How meals can evoke personal and family memories.

children.title: Unit 6: Plan for Yourself
children.content: Discusses future plans, dream jobs, and making resolutions.

children.title: Future with be going to
children.content: Using be going to to talk about plans and intentions.

children.title: Affirmative Statements
children.content: e.g., I am going to study law.

children.title: Questions and Negatives
children.content: e.g., Are you going to...? I am not going to...

children.title: Dream Jobs
children.content: Aspirational careers and how to achieve them.

children.title: Career Vocabulary
children.content: Words for jobs like engineer, musician, doctor, etc.

children.title: Path to Achievement
children.content: Steps needed to reach career goals, e.g., study, practice.

children.title: Resolutions
children.content: Promises to oneself for self-improvement, often at the New Year.

children.title: Types of Resolutions
children.content: e.g., health, learning, habits.

children.title: Keeping Resolutions
children.content: Strategies for sticking to goals, like setting mini-goals.

children.title: Unit 7: When Tomorrow Comes
children.content: Focuses on future predictions, technology, and preparation for the future.

children.title: Future with will
children.content: Using will for predictions and spontaneous decisions about the future.

children.title: Predictions
children.content: e.g., Robots will do housework.

children.title: Yes/No Questions
children.content: e.g., Will people live longer?

children.title: Technological Advances
children.content: How technology might change life in the future.

children.title: AI and Robotics
children.content: The role of artificial intelligence and robots.

children.title: Smart Homes
children.content: Homes with automated systems for convenience.

children.title: Preparing for the Future
children.content: Skills and attitudes needed for future success.

children.title: Lifelong Learning
children.content: The importance of continuous education.

children.title: Adaptability
children.content: Being open to change and new challenges.

children.title: Unit 8: Let's Communicate!
children.content: Covers communication methods, conversation skills, and conditionals.

children.title: Communication Methods
children.content: Different ways to communicate, e.g., face-to-face, phone, text.

children.title: Verbal Communication
children.content: Speaking directly or via calls.

children.title: Non-verbal Cues
children.content: Body language and facial expressions.

children.title: Zero and First Conditionals
children.content: Conditional sentences for real situations.

children.title: Zero Conditional
children.content: For general truths, e.g., If you heat ice, it melts.

children.title: First Conditional
children.content: For likely future events, e.g., If it rains, we will stay home.

children.title: Effective Communication
children.content: Tips for better conversations, like listening and being sincere.

children.title: Active Listening
children.content: Paying full attention and showing interest.

children.title: Appropriate Topics
children.content: Choosing subjects that are polite and engaging.
